story.title: OpenAI Files Counter Lawsuit Against Apple Over Trade Secrets
story.summary: OpenAI has filed a counter lawsuit against Apple, alleging that the tech giant has set up departing employees to be accused of stealing trade secrets. This legal action comes amid escalating tensions between the two companies as competition in the artificial intelligence sector intensifies.

explore_lenses.label: Why does this fight matter for AI hardware?
explore_lenses.title: A dispute over the next consumer device market
explore_lenses.summary: The case reaches beyond employee departures: both companies are positioning for AI-enabled consumer hardware, where control of suppliers, product plans and engineering talent can determine who brings new devices to market.

claims.text: OpenAI alleges that Apple discouraged hardware suppliers from working on future OpenAI devices and says its planned AI-enabled personal electronics could compete directly with Apple.

Apple's original complaint alleges that former employees' confidential knowledge could help OpenAI shortcut hardware research, manufacturing development and supplier relationships as it enters consumer devices.

Apple's July suit names OpenAI, io Products and former Apple employees Chang Liu and Tang Yew Tan; Tan is OpenAI's chief hardware officer and previously spent 24 years at Apple, according to the reporting and court complaint.

explore_lenses.label: How did the Apple-OpenAI dispute escalate?
explore_lenses.title: From employee exits to competing accusations
explore_lenses.summary: Apple first accused OpenAI and former Apple staff of taking confidential hardware information. OpenAI denied seeking Apple secrets, criticized Apple's offboarding practices, and has now brought counterclaims alleging Apple obtained OpenAI information through a rehired former employee.

claims.text: Apple filed its federal complaint on July 10, 2026, alleging trade-secret misappropriation and breach of confidentiality agreements by Liu, Tan, OpenAI and io Products.

Apple alleges Liu and Tan accessed or used proprietary information to assist OpenAI's hardware work, obtain insider knowledge during recruiting, and instruct hires on avoiding scrutiny when leaving Apple.

OpenAI says Apple's systems can leave departing workers with residual access to files and maintains that it neither has nor wants Apple's trade secrets; it characterizes Apple's suit as based on false information.
In its November 27 counterclaims, OpenAI alleged that Apple obtained confidential OpenAI device and product-roadmap information through a former OpenAI employee whom Apple rehired.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in court?
explore_lenses.title: Discovery will test the competing accounts
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate legal focus is evidence preservation and targeted discovery, not a final ruling on whose narrative is correct. The court has permitted some accelerated fact-gathering while rejecting or deferring other requests as too broad or insufficiently defined.

claims.text: On October 13, 2026, the Northern District of California granted Apple limited expedited discovery, including specified document requests and depositions of Liu, Tan, Alyssa Peng and corporate representatives of OpenAI and io.

The court denied expedited requests seeking broad documents about OpenAI's research and development on metal finishes, power management and battery functionality, directing that such matters proceed through ordinary merits discovery.
The court expressly declined at that stage to weigh the parties' competing forensic-expert accounts concerning alleged use, deletion or restoration of files.
Apple's requested preliminary injunction remains a central procedural issue; discovery was allowed in part because the court found a connection between certain forensic evidence and that request.

story_report.summary: OpenAI has filed counterclaims against Apple in a trade-secrets dispute, alleging that Apple’s handling of departing workers has set them up to face accusations of taking confidential information. OpenAI also alleges that Apple obtained confidential information about its device plans through a former OpenAI employee whom Apple rehired. The filing broadens a federal case that began with Apple’s claims over former employees and OpenAI’s hardware ambitions, while the companies compete in artificial intelligence and consumer devices.

sections.heading: Apple’s Original Trade-Secrets Complaint
sections.body: Apple filed its federal complaint on July 10, 2026, accusing OpenAI, io Products, and former Apple employees Chang Liu and Tang Yew Tan of trade-secret misappropriation and breaches of confidentiality agreements. Apple alleges that confidential knowledge from the employees could help OpenAI accelerate hardware research, manufacturing development and supplier relationships. Tan, OpenAI’s chief hardware officer, previously spent 24 years at Apple, according to reporting and the complaint.

sections.heading: OpenAI Challenges Apple’s Account
sections.body: OpenAI says Apple’s systems can leave departing employees with residual access to files and maintains that it neither has nor wants Apple trade secrets, calling Apple’s case based on false information. Its counterclaims also accuse Apple of discouraging hardware suppliers from working on future OpenAI devices. OpenAI says its planned AI-enabled personal electronics could compete directly with Apple’s products.

sections.heading: Court Allows Limited Early Discovery
sections.body: On October 13, the Northern District of California authorized limited expedited discovery, including specified document requests and depositions involving Liu, Tan, Alyssa Peng, OpenAI and io representatives. The court declined Apple’s request for broad early discovery into OpenAI research on metal finishes, power management and battery functionality, directing those issues to ordinary merits discovery. Apple’s request for a preliminary injunction remains pending.

unresolved.text: The court has not resolved whether either company possessed or used the other’s trade secrets, whether alleged supplier conduct was unlawful, or whether Apple will receive a preliminary injunction. It also declined at this stage to weigh competing forensic-expert accounts over the alleged use, deletion or restoration of files.

related_stories.title: Efforts Underway to Prevent Oil Spill from Capsized Tanker near Ibiza
related_stories.summary: A tanker carrying 7,000 tonnes of diesel has capsized off the coast of Ibiza, prompting urgent action from Spanish authorities to prevent an oil spill. While there are concerns about potential ecological damage, the ship's fuel tanks remain intact. One person has been reported dead in the incident.

related_stories.title: Severe Thanksgiving Storm Causes Widespread Flooding and Power Outages
related_stories.summary: A powerful storm impacted the East Coast during Thanksgiving, resulting in significant flooding and widespread power outages. Nearly 1 million customers experienced power loss, with reports indicating that around 940,000 were affected at the peak of the outages. Cleanup efforts are underway as millions deal with the aftermath of the storm, which brought heavy rain and high winds, toppling trees and flooding streets.

related_stories.title: Zelenskyy Criticizes Trump's 'Friend' Remark About Putin, Urges US Pressure
related_stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed frustration over the U.S. approach to Russia, particularly criticizing Donald Trump's comment referring to Vladimir Putin as 'my friend.' Zelenskyy likened this remark to calling Adolf Hitler a friend during World War II, emphasizing that Putin is an aggressor and should not be viewed as a friend. His comments come amid ongoing tensions related to military support and financial aid for Ukraine.

related_stories.title: Republicans Consider Revising Tariffs Amid Democratic Challenges
related_stories.summary: In the wake of significant election losses, many Republicans are expressing a willingness to reconsider tariffs that have been a key part of Trump's trade agenda. This shift may provide Democrats with an opportunity to challenge the existing tariff policies as they gain control of Congress.
